title: Problem 1.1
statement_text: Given a hereditary property $\mathcal{P}$ which misses a bipartite graph and a $(c,t)$-sparse graph $\Gamma$, determine $\mathrm{ex}(\Gamma,\mathcal{P})$.
context_text: A graph $\Gamma$ on $n$ vertices is $(c,t)$-sparse if for all vertex subsets $A,B$ (not necessarily disjoint) with $|A|,|B|\ge t$ we have $e(A,B)\le(1-c)|A||B|$, where $e(A,B)$ counts the pairs $(a,b)\in A\times B$ with $ab\in E(\Gamma)$. A hereditary property is a class of graphs closed under induced subgraphs; it is assumed nontrivial (contains all edgeless graphs and misses some graph). For a hereditary property $\mathcal{P}$, $\mathrm{ex}(\Gamma,\mathcal{P})$ is the maximum number of edges of a subgraph $G\subseteq\Gamma$ that belongs to $\mathcal{P}$; for a graph $H$, $\mathcal{P}_H$ is the property of not containing $H$ as an induced subgraph. For $\Gamma=K_n$ and the property of not containing $H$ as a subgraph, this is the usual Turán number. The random graph $G(n,p)$ with fixed $0<p<1$ is with high probability $(c,t)$-sparse for any fixed $c<1-p$ and $t\ge C'\log n$, and a graph is $K_{t,t}$-free if and only if it is $(1/t^2,t)$-sparse, so the problem unifies Turán problems in dense random or pseudorandom hosts and induced Turán problems in $K_{t,t}$-free graphs. Alon, Krivelevich and Samotij asked to show $\mathrm{ex}(G(n,p),\mathcal{P})\le n^{2-\varepsilon}$ when $\mathcal{P}$ misses a bipartite graph. Calling a bipartite graph $H=(A\cup B,E)$ $d$-bounded if some $1\le\ell\le d$ vertices of $A$ are complete to $B$ and all other vertices of $A$ have degree at most $d$, the authors prove that every subgraph of a $(c,t)$-sparse $\Gamma$ with at least $Ct^{1/d}n^{2-1/d}$ edges contains a copy of $H$ that is induced in $\Gamma$, which answers that question; they determine $\mathrm{ex}(\Gamma,\mathcal{P}_H)$ up to a constant factor for trees $H$ and for suitable $K_{s,r}$ when $\Gamma$ is a dense random graph or a Paley graph with a square number of vertices.
paper_title: The largest subgraph without a forbidden induced subgraph

title: Conjecture 6.1
statement_text: For every $c>0$ and integer $\ell$ there exists $C>1$, such that if $\Gamma$ is a $(c,t)$-sparse graph then $\mathrm{ex}(\Gamma,\mathcal{P}_{C_{2\ell}})\leq Ct^{1-1/\ell}n^{1+1/\ell}$.
context_text: A graph $\Gamma$ on $n$ vertices is $(c,t)$-sparse if for all vertex subsets $A,B$ (not necessarily disjoint) with $|A|,|B|\ge t$ we have $e(A,B)\le(1-c)|A||B|$, where $e(A,B)$ counts the pairs $(a,b)\in A\times B$ with $ab\in E(\Gamma)$. A hereditary property is a class of graphs closed under induced subgraphs; it is assumed nontrivial (contains all edgeless graphs and misses some graph). For a hereditary property $\mathcal{P}$, $\mathrm{ex}(\Gamma,\mathcal{P})$ is the maximum number of edges of a subgraph $G\subseteq\Gamma$ that belongs to $\mathcal{P}$; for a graph $H$, $\mathcal{P}_H$ is the property of not containing $H$ as an induced subgraph. For $\Gamma=K_n$ and the property of not containing $H$ as a subgraph, this is the usual Turán number. The authors give the general lower bound $\mathrm{ex}(\Gamma,\mathcal{P}_H)\ge\frac12e(\Gamma)\,\mathrm{ex}(\chi(\overline{\Gamma}),\mathcal{F}_H)/\binom{\chi(\overline{\Gamma})}{2}$, where a clique quotient of $H$ is the graph obtained by contracting each part of a partition of $V(H)$ into cliques, and $\mathcal{F}_H$ is the family of bipartite clique quotients of $H$. For $H=C_{2\ell}$, $\mathcal{F}_H$ consists of all cycles of length between $\ell$ and $2\ell$, and graphs on $n$ vertices of girth larger than $2\ell$ have at most $\frac12n^{1+1/\ell}+\frac12n$ edges (Alon, Hoory and Linial), a bound conjectured to be tight up to a constant factor and known to be so for $\ell\in\{2,3,5\}$. This motivates the conjectured upper bound. For comparison, the authors prove $\mathrm{ex}(\Gamma,\mathcal{P}_T)\le Ctn$ for every tree $T$, which is tight.

title: Conjecture 6.2
statement_text: For every $c>0$ and a graph $H$, there exists $C>1$ such that if $\Gamma$ is a $(c,t)$-sparse graph then $\mathrm{ex}(\Gamma,\mathcal{D}_{H})\leq Ctn$.
context_text: Here $\mathcal{D}_{H}$ denotes the property of not containing a subdivision of $H$ as an induced subgraph. The conjecture predicts a linear (in $n$) upper bound, up to the factor $t$, for the induced subdivision Turán number in $(c,t)$-sparse graphs, for any fixed graph $H$.
